name: Jump squat, tuck and split jumps
pattern: Vertical jump from a quick squat dip: hips, knees and ankles extend together, then land softly and reload.
setup: Feet hip to shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Chest up, arms ready to swing (or hands on hips, or holding the load).
Weight over the middle of your feet.

steps.text: Swing your arms back and sink quickly to about a half squat.
Drive the floor away and swing your arms up; leave the ground with straight legs and pointed toes.
Land on the balls of your feet, roll to flat and bend hips and knees to absorb.
Stand tall, or go straight into the next jump.

cues.cue: Land soft and quiet, like a spring.
cues.why: Bending knees and hips at landing reduces impact; taught landers make lower forces.

cues.cue: Knees out over your toes on take-off and landing.
cues.why: Knee valgus on landing predicts ACL injury; female athletes show more of it.
An arm swing raises jump height through several combined effects.

cues.cue: Full extension: hips, knees, ankles straight at take-off.
cues.why: The jump squat and power clean share this extension pattern.
A fast stretch-shortening cycle improves power; a long pause wastes it.

breathing: Breathe in on the dip, out on the jump; keep breathing in fast sets.

tempo.note: Explosive. For power: 3-6 reps with full rest. For conditioning: continuous jumps in intervals.

mistakes.name: Stiff landing
mistakes.looks: Legs nearly straight at contact and a loud landing.
mistakes.fix: Land toes-to-heels and sink into the next dip.
mistakes.why: Higher impact on knees and back.

mistakes.name: Knees cave in
mistakes.looks: Knees move toward each other on take-off or landing.
mistakes.fix: Spread the floor with your feet; jump lower until it is clean.
mistakes.why: Knee valgus on landing links to ACL injury.

mistakes.name: Chest collapses
mistakes.looks: The torso folds forward on landing, heels lift.
mistakes.fix: Chest up, hips back, weight mid-foot.
mistakes.why: Moves load to the lower back and toes.

mistakes.name: Uneven landing
mistakes.looks: One foot lands first or the feet land at different spots.
mistakes.fix: Jump lower and aim for one sound on landing.
mistakes.why: Asymmetric landing is a scored error in landing screens.

safety: Loaded jump squats: keep the load light (well under a third of your squat max) and land softly.
Knee or Achilles pain: switch to box jumps (lower landing force) or squats.
Plyometrics on fresh legs; stop when landings get loud.

variants.change: Holding a load: smaller jump, same landing rules.
Band under the feet resists the jump.
Holding suspension straps for help and balance.
Continuous squat jumps in intervals: about 11.0 MET (02214).

subtypes.name: Split jump
subtypes.change: Lunge stance, jump and switch legs in the air, land in a soft lunge.

subtypes.name: Tuck jump
subtypes.change: Jump high and pull both knees to the chest at the peak, then open up before landing.

subtypes.name: Pogo and calf jumps
subtypes.change: Small, fast bounces off the balls of the feet with knees nearly straight; the ankles do the work.

subtypes.name: Single-leg jump
subtypes.match: single leg|one leg|pistol|2 to 1|1 to 2|two to one
subtypes.change: Take off and land on one leg; free knee bent, much lower jump height.

subtypes.name: Jump with a turn
subtypes.change: Same jump with a turn or a change of foot position in the air.

motion.basis: Landing targets from padua2009 and herrington2010 ranges; valgus risk from hewett2005 and ford2003; arm swing from lees2004; extension pattern from mackenzie2014. Keyframe angles are estimates. Conditioning MET 7.5 is Compendium 02020 (vigorous calisthenics); interval use 11.0 (02214).
